issue.title: Custom element 'Array/Object' props Bug

repository.name: core
repository.description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.

issue.body:
### Version
3.2.4

### Reproduction link
[https://codesandbox.io/s/vue-3-2-custom-element-array-bug-sqpip](https://codesandbox.io/s/vue-3-2-custom-element-array-bug-sqpip)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Define component
```javascript
const CustomSelect = Vue.defineCustomElement({
    props: {
        options: Array
    },
    template: `
      <select :value="value" @input="clicked">
        <option
            v-for="option in options"
            :key="option"
            :value="option"
        >
          {{ option }}
        </option>
      </select>`,
});

customElements.define('custom-select', CustomSelect);
```
2. Use component
```html
<custom-select options="['1', '2', '3']" value="1"/>
```
3. Show in console
```bash
[Vue warn]: Invalid prop: type check failed for prop "options". Expected Array, got String with value "['1', '2', '3']". 
  at <CustomSelect options="['1', '2', '3']" value="1" >
```

### What is expected?
Convert the value of the 'options' prop to an Array.

### What is actually happening?
The prop type 'Array' is ignored.

### Steps to reproduce
Clone the repo provided

1. npm run install

2. npm run build:demo

3. cd demo

4. npx http-server

### What is expected?
Value passed in as prop starting with number should not be treated as numbers unless that's the entire value.

### What is actually happening?
Value passed in starting with a number is being parsed as number and rest of the value is being ignored

---
I was building a custom element library.

issue.title: fix(custom-elements): cast numbers with Number rules

repository.name: core
repository.description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.

issue.body:
Fix #4370

By using `Number()`, we handle Infinity, NaN, and all other number syntaxes. I think this makes the most sense for the custom elements since it's also _"the platform"_ and Infinity and NaN can be conveniently casted to a string too (`String(Number('Infinity')) === 'Infinity')`).

We could also take a look at the type of the prop being a Number and only apply the cast in that case. Let me know if that makes more sense.

issue.title: Custom element - Prop String will be parsed to a Number

repository.name: core
repository.description: 🖖 Vue.js is a progressive, incrementally-adoptable JavaScript framework for building UI on the web.

issue.body:
### Version
3.2.6

### Reproduction link
[https://codesandbox.io/s/black-butterfly-egj7x?file=/src/main.js](https://codesandbox.io/s/black-butterfly-egj7x?file=/src/main.js)







### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a defineCustomElement with two props (language, externalId) from type String
2. Insert the custom element into a html page and define the attributes as follows:

language="de" externalid="4332cdd-3243443d22"
3. The prop externalId is parsed to a number and contains the value 4332

### What is expected?
The prop from type String should not be parsed to a number and the component should receive the exact same value

### What is actually happening?
The prop externalId from type String is automatically parsed to a number
